title: SAP: ERP, HANA and Business Objects

videos.script: Serra Alta's books, its sales and its milk receipts all live in one system. {{title}} It is SAP, and nobody in this course will log on to it. SAP sells to companies, not to people. So this lesson teaches it the way an architect meets it: from the documentation, and from the team that runs it. {{landscape}} Joana spends a week with Edson Prado's SAP team. She learns that SAP here is three systems, not one. A change is made in development, tested in quality, and only then moved into production. {{hana}} Then the date that sets the agenda. SAP stops mainstream support for ECC at the end of 2027. Its successor, S/4HANA, runs on a column-oriented database, and it changed the data model underneath. So the move is a project of years, not an upgrade. {{doors}} Next, the four published ways into SAP, and why its tables are not one of them, even for reading. {{reports}} Last, the reports. Nine hundred of them, and a third nobody opened in a year. By the end you will know where SAP's edges are. That is what you design around.
